rationale: The fixed experiment e928fb3f495f4de9a5d56bef8b4c66e0-experiment has been executed and retained, so this update converts the last-voter removal probe into an execution-grounded conclusion for question e928fb3f495f4de9a5d56bef8b4c66e0-question-0 and records the observed instance as durable knowledge: the proposal was accepted and committed, and applying the committed entry aborted the applying node with the changer's own 'removed all voters' error text, while the add-voter control applied cleanly. The question is marked explained with the sourced behavior entry as its premise, and the deliberate changer-level rejection, the deliberate panic in the apply path, the single-voter scope and the unobserved process-level consequences stay in the counterevidence and limitations.

knowledge.assertion: The propose path does not check the resulting voter set and the apply path converts the changer's error into a panic, which is what the execution observed end to end.

knowledge.statement: In the retained execution of the fixed experiment (single-voter cluster {1}, node 1 made leader in term 1 with committed 1 and applied 0, fault-free in-process), proposing a ConfChangeV2 that removes node 1 through MsgProp returned no error (parsed index 1: proposal_error '<nil>') and the entry was appended at index 2 and committed (committed true); applying that committed entry through the documented application path panicked with the verbatim recovered value 'removed all voters' and left the configuration unchanged (index 1: panicked true, recovered 'removed all voters', voters_after [1], node_state StateLeader). The control probe with an add-voter change of the same shape was accepted and committed the same way and applied without aborting (parsed index 3: panicked false, recovered empty, voters_after [1,2]).
knowledge.conditions: One executed in-process experiment with the fixed harness bytes of experiment e928fb3f495f4de9a5d56bef8b4c66e0-experiment (receipt 6c7f22d449564006a909a218643cfe08, exit 0, changed_target_files [], no parsing errors); a single-voter configuration, a direct becomeCandidate/becomeLeader setup, the proposal delivered as a MsgProp carrying an EntryConfChangeV2, and the application path modelled as a direct ApplyConfChange call with a recovering wrapper. One observed instance under these conditions, not a universal guarantee.

interpretations.rationale: Receipt 6c7f22d449564006a909a218643cfe08 is a completed execution of this investigation's own experiment (status completed, exit 0, outcome tests_passed, unchanged target files, no parsing errors, 4 parsed events). Comparison 0 declares that applying a committed conf change that removes the last voter does not abort the applying node; it is violated with a complete valid witness at parsed index 1, correlated to its own admission at index 0 (conf_change_setup for probe remove-last-voter: voters_before [1], pendingConfIndex 0, applied 0, committed 1, node_state StateLeader, term 1). The measured operands at index 1 are proposal_error '<nil>', proposed_index 2, committed true, panicked true, recovered 'removed all voters', voters_after [1] and node_state StateLeader, so the sequence is: the proposal was accepted with no error, the entry committed, the application path aborted on the committed entry, and the configuration stayed unchanged. Comparison 1 is the control of the same shape and holds at index 3: the add-voter change was accepted and committed identically and applied with panicked false and voters_after [1,2], which shows the path, the commit step and the apply call are functional and that the abort is specific to the change that empties the voter set. The mechanism is the sourced one: the changer returns the error 'removed all voters' only when it computes the resulting configuration (confchange/confchange.go:170-172, an expected changer-level rejection per confchange/testdata/simple_safety.txt), the leader's propose-time validation never computes that result and therefore accepts the proposal (raft.go:1318-1335), and raft.applyConfChange converts any changer error into a panic with a TODO to return it to the caller (raft.go:1961-1964). Engineering significance: an action available to a client through the documented proposal interface is accepted and made durable before the node that applies it aborts, so the abort happens after the decision rather than instead of it; the committed entry also remains in the log, which raises the restart question recorded as a limitation rather than as an observation.

knowledge.assertion: The proposal passes the propose-time validation and commits (index 0/1: pendingConfIndex 0, proposal_error nil, committed true) and the apply path panics with the changer's error text (index 1: recovered 'removed all voters').

counterevidence: The changer-level rejection is deliberate and tested: confchange/testdata/simple_safety.txt expects 'removed all voters' for such changes, so the captured library treats an empty voter set as an invalid configuration rather than a supported one; the question is where the rejection surfaces, not whether the configuration is rejected.

The panic in applyConfChange is also deliberate: the captured code panics with an explicit TODO to return the error to the caller, so a reviewer may read the abort as an intentional 'impossible state' guard reached only because an embedding application proposed an invalid change.

The control probe (index 3) shows the same path applies a valid change normally, so the abort depends on the proposed change emptying the voter set rather than on the harness, the commit step or the apply call.

A single-voter cluster is the degenerate configuration in which a legal client request can empty the voter set; in larger clusters the same error requires a change that removes every voter at once, which a client can also express.
The harness recovered the panic itself and applied the entry directly; the process-level consequence, the behaviour of a full server loop and any restart behaviour were not observed.
limitations: Single-voter configuration and one executed instance; other cluster sizes and multi-node atomic changes were not probed.

The committed entry stays in the log after the abort, so a restart would re-apply it; whether that produces a repeated abort or is prevented by the embedding application's persisted applied index is not observed here.
The application path was modelled as a direct ApplyConfChange call with a recovering wrapper instead of a full Ready/Advance loop.

Whether an embedding service is expected to validate the resulting voter set before proposing is a contract question outside the captured package, so the severity and defect classification remain with human review.
This interpretation concerns the proposal-to-apply sequence; the earlier silent-replacement finding on the same validation block is about a different branch and is unaffected.
interpretations.report_title: 客户端可提议“移除最后一个 voter”并被提交，应用该条目时节点 panic（该变更事后才被拒绝）
interpretations.report_answer: 在快照代码上，单 voter 集群 {1} 中通过 MsgProp 提议移除 node 1：Step 返回 nil，条目写入索引 2 并提交（committed=true），随后按文档应用该已提交条目时 panic，recovered 文本为 'removed all voters'，配置保持 [1] 未变；对照的加节点变更为同样形状（提议成功、提交、应用无 panic，voters 变为 [1,2]）。源码显示拒绝发生在 changer 计算最终配置时（confchange/confchange.go:170-172，且该错误在 confchange/testdata/simple_safety.txt 中被当作预期行为），提议阶段的校验不计算最终 voter 集合（raft.go:1318-1335），而 applyConfChange 把任何 changer 错误直接 panic（raft.go:1961-1964，附 TODO 要求改为返回错误）。因此“拒绝”发生在提交与写入日志之后，进程级与重启后的后果未在本实验中观测，是否构成缺陷需人工结合调用方契约复核。
